sanskrit: citādhūmena nīlena saṃrajyante ca pādapāḥ śmaśāne ca nirāhārāḥ pratinandanti dehinaḥ
english: The trees here are stained dark by the smoke of the pyres, and in this charnel-ground the creatures that haunt it, foodless and lean, rejoice at the prospect of a corpse.

sanskrit: sarve vikrāntavīryāś ca asmin deśe sudāruṇāḥ yuṣmān pradharṣayiṣyanti vikṛtā māṃsabhojanāḥ
english: All of them are bold in their might and most terrible in this place; misshapen flesh-eaters, they will fall upon you and overpower you.

sanskrit: dūrāc cāyaṃ vanoddeśo bhayam atra bhaviṣyati tyajyatāṃ kāṣṭhabhūto 'yaṃ mṛṣyatāṃ jāmbukaṃ vacaḥ
english: This stretch of wilderness lies far off, and here danger will arise. Abandon this body that has become mere wood; do not heed the jackal's words.

sanskrit: yadi jambukavākyāni niṣphalāny anṛtāni ca śroṣyatha bhraṣṭavijñānās tataḥ sarve vinaṅkṣyatha
english: If, with your judgment fallen away, you listen to the jackal's words, which are barren and false, then you will all be undone.

sanskrit: jambuka uvāca sthīyatāṃ neha bhetavyaṃ yāvat tapati bhāskaraḥ tāvad asmin sutasnehād anirvedena vartata
english: The jackal said: Stay here, and do not be afraid. So long as the sun still burns, abide here for love of your son, without despair.

sanskrit: svairaṃ rudata visrabdhāḥ svairaṃ snehena paśyata sthīyatāṃ yāvad ādityaḥ kiṃ vaḥ kravyādabhāṣitaiḥ
english: Weep your fill, untroubled; gaze your fill with love upon him. Stay while the sun yet stands—what are the words of a flesh-eater to you?

sanskrit: yadi gṛdhrasya vākyāni tīvrāṇi rabhasāni ca gṛhṇīta mohitātmānaḥ suto vo na bhaviṣyati
english: If, your minds bewildered, you accept the vulture's words—harsh and headlong as they are—your son will be no more to you.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca gṛdhro 'nastamite tv āha gate 'stam iti jambukaḥ mṛtasya taṃ parijanam ūcatus tau kṣudhānvitau
english: Bhīṣma said: The vulture said the sun had not yet set; the jackal said it had gone down. So those two, driven by hunger, spoke to the dead child's kin.

sanskrit: svakāryadakṣiṇau rājan gṛdhro jambuka eva ca kṣutpipāsāpariśrāntau śāstram ālambya jalpataḥ
english: O king, both the vulture and the jackal, each shrewd in his own cause, worn out by hunger and thirst, kept arguing, each leaning upon scripture for support.

sanskrit: tayor vijñānaviduṣor dvayor jambukapatriṇoḥ vākyair amṛtakalpair hi prātiṣṭhanta vrajanti ca
english: At the words—sweet as nectar—of those two learned in cunning, the jackal and the winged one, the people now made to set out, now turned to go.

sanskrit: śokadainyasamāviṣṭā rudantas tasthire tadā svakāryakuśalābhyāṃ te saṃbhrāmyante ha naipuṇāt
english: Sunk in grief and misery, weeping, they then stood still, kept whirling this way and that by the practiced skill of those two who each pursued his own ends.

sanskrit: tathā tayor vivadator vijñānaviduṣor dvayoḥ bāndhavānāṃ sthitānāṃ ca upātiṣṭhata śaṃkaraḥ
english: While those two cunning ones thus wrangled on, and the kinsmen stood there waiting, Śaṃkara drew near.

sanskrit: tatas tān āha manujān varado 'smīti śūlabhṛt te pratyūcur idaṃ vākyaṃ duḥkhitāḥ praṇatāḥ sthitāḥ
english: Then the Trident-bearer, granter of boons, said to those men, 'I am here to grant a boon.' Grieving, bowed low, they stood and answered him these words.

sanskrit: ekaputravihīnānāṃ sarveṣāṃ jīvitārthinām putrasya no jīvadānāj jīvitaṃ dātum arhasi
english: 'We have all lost our only son and long to go on living; by giving life back to our son, you would be giving life to us.'

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa bhagavān vāripūrṇena pāṇinā jīvaṃ tasmai kumārāya prādād varṣaśatāya vai
english: Thus addressed, the blessed Lord, with a palm full of water, granted that boy his life, to last a hundred years.

sanskrit: tathā gomāyugṛdhrābhyām adadat kṣudvināśanam varaṃ pinākī bhagavān sarvabhūtahite rataḥ
english: And to the jackal and the vulture the blessed bearer of the Pināka, ever devoted to the welfare of all beings, gave the boon of the ending of their hunger.

sanskrit: tataḥ praṇamya taṃ devaṃ śreyoharṣasamanvitāḥ kṛtakṛtyāḥ sukhaṃ hṛṣṭāḥ prātiṣṭhanta tadā vibho
english: Then, O lord, bowing to that god, filled with joy at their good fortune, their purpose fulfilled, glad and at ease, they set out for home.

sanskrit: anirvedena dīrgheṇa niścayena dhruveṇa ca devadevaprasādāc ca kṣipraṃ phalam avāpyate
english: By unwavering, long-sustained perseverance, by firm resolve, and by the grace of the God of gods, the fruit is swiftly won.

sanskrit: paśya devasya saṃyogaṃ bāndhavānāṃ ca niścayam kṛpaṇānāṃ hi rudatāṃ kṛtam aśrupramārjanam
english: See how the god's coming and the kinsmen's resolve together wiped away the tears of those wretched mourners.

sanskrit: paśya cālpena kālena niścayānveṣaṇena ca prasādaṃ śaṃkarāt prāpya duḥkhitāḥ sukham āpnuvan
english: And see how in a short time, through resolve and persistent seeking, those grieving ones, having won Śaṃkara's grace, attained their joy.

sanskrit: te vismitāḥ prahṛṣṭāś ca putrasaṃjīvanāt punaḥ babhūvur bharataśreṣṭha prasādāc chaṃkarasya vai
english: Amazed and overjoyed at the bringing back to life of their son, O best of the Bhāratas, they were made glad once more by the grace of Śaṃkara.

sanskrit: tatas te tvaritā rājañ śrutvā śokam aghodbhavam viviśuḥ putram ādāya nagaraṃ hṛṣṭamānasāḥ eṣā buddhiḥ samastānāṃ cāturvarṇye nidarśitā
english: Then, O king, having known a grief born of calamity, they made haste and, taking up their son, entered the city with glad hearts. Such is the wisdom set forth for all men within the four orders of society.

sanskrit: dharmārthamokṣasaṃyuktam itihāsam imaṃ śubham śrutvā manuṣyaḥ satatam iha pretya ca modate
english: By hearing this auspicious tale, bound up with dharma, worldly gain, and liberation, a man rejoices forever, both here and after death.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam saṃvādaṃ bharataśreṣṭha śalmaleḥ pavanasya ca
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they tell an ancient tale, O best of the Bhāratas—the dialogue between the silk-cotton tree and the Wind.

sanskrit: himavantaṃ samāsādya mahān āsīd vanaspatiḥ varṣapūgābhisaṃvṛddhaḥ śākhāskandhapalāśavān
english: On the slopes of the Himālaya there stood a mighty forest-lord, grown great over a host of years, rich in branches, trunk, and foliage.

sanskrit: tatra sma mattā mātaṅgā dharmārtāḥ śramakarśitāḥ viśramanti mahābāho tathānyā mṛgajātayaḥ
english: There, O mighty-armed one, rutting elephants, oppressed by the heat and worn out with toil, would rest, and so too the other tribes of wild creatures.

sanskrit: nalvamātraparīṇāho ghanacchāyo vanaspatiḥ śukaśārikasaṃghuṣṭaḥ phalavān puṣpavān api
english: A bowshot in girth, with dense shade, the forest-lord was loud with parrots and mynahs, laden with fruit and laden with flowers.

sanskrit: sārthikā vaṇijaś cāpi tāpasāś ca vanaukasaḥ vasanti vāsān mārgasthāḥ suramye tarusattame
english: Caravan-folk and merchants, ascetics and forest-dwellers, travelers upon the road, would take their lodging in that loveliest, most excellent of trees.

sanskrit: tasyā tā vipulāḥ śākhā dṛṣṭvā skandhāṃś ca sarvataḥ abhigamyābravīd enaṃ nārado bharatarṣabha
english: Seeing its broad branches and its trunks on every side, Nārada drew near and addressed it, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: aho nu ramaṇīyas tvam aho cāsi manoramaḥ prīyāmahe tvayā nityaṃ tarupravara śalmale
english: 'Ah, how delightful you are, and ah, how you charm the heart! We take everlasting joy in you, O silk-cotton tree, foremost of trees.'

sanskrit: sadaiva śakunās tāta mṛgāś cādhas tathā gajāḥ vasanti tava saṃhṛṣṭā manoharatarās tathā
english: 'Forever, dear one, the birds, and below the deer and the elephants, dwell about you full of delight, and grow the more charming for it.'

sanskrit: tava śākhā mahāśākha skandhaṃ ca vipulaṃ tathā na vai prabhagnān paśyāmi mārutena kathaṃ cana
english: 'Your branches, O great-branched one, and your broad trunk as well—nowhere do I see them broken by the wind in any way.'

sanskrit: kiṃ nu te mārutas tāta prītimān atha vā suhṛt tvāṃ rakṣati sadā yena vane 'smin pavano dhruvam
english: 'Is the wind, then, dear one, fond of you, or your friend, that the Breeze should always protect you so surely here in this forest?'

sanskrit: vivān hi pavanaḥ sthānād vṛkṣān uccāvacān api parvatānāṃ ca śikharāṇy ācālayati vegavān
english: 'For the wind, blowing in its force, shakes trees great and small from their place, and the very peaks of mountains.'

sanskrit: śoṣayaty eva pātālaṃ vivān gandhavahaḥ śuciḥ hradāṃś ca saritaś caiva sāgarāṃś ca tathaiva ha
english: 'The pure bearer of scents, blowing on, dries up the very netherworld—the deep pools, the rivers, and the seas as well.'

sanskrit: tvāṃ saṃrakṣeta pavanaḥ sakhitvena na saṃśayaḥ tasmād bahalaśākho 'si parṇavān puṣpavān api
english: 'Surely the wind protects you out of friendship, no doubt of it; and so you are thick with branches, full of leaves and full of flowers.'

sanskrit: idaṃ ca ramaṇīyaṃ te pratibhāti vanaspate yad ime vihagās tāta ramante muditās tvayi
english: 'And this seems delightful in you, O forest-lord—that these birds, dear one, take their joy in you, glad at heart.'

sanskrit: eṣāṃ pṛthak samastānāṃ śrūyate madhuraḥ svaraḥ puṣpasaṃmodane kāle vāśatāṃ sumanoharam
english: 'Sweet is the voice heard of them, each apart and all together, as they cry out most charmingly in the season of the rejoicing of the flowers.'

sanskrit: tatheme muditā nāgāḥ svayūthakulaśobhinaḥ gharmārtās tvāṃ samāsādya sukhaṃ vindanti śalmale
english: 'And these glad elephants, the pride of their own herds and lineages, when reaching you in the torment of the heat, find their ease, O silk-cotton tree.'

sanskrit: tathaiva mṛgajātībhir anyābhir upaśobhase tathā sārthādhivāsaiś ca śobhase meruvad druma
english: 'And likewise you are adorned by other tribes of wild creatures, and adorned by the dwelling of caravans, O tree—so that you shine like Meru.'

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaiś ca tapaḥsiddhais tāpasaiḥ śramaṇair api triviṣṭapasamaṃ manye tavāyatanam eva ha
english: 'With brahmins perfected in austerity, with ascetics and with wandering mendicants, I deem your abode the very equal of heaven.'

sanskrit: bandhutvād atha vā sakhyāc chalmale nātra saṃśayaḥ pālayaty eva satataṃ bhīmaḥ sarvatrago 'nilaḥ
english: 'Out of kinship or out of friendship, O silk-cotton tree—of this there is no doubt—the terrible, all-pervading wind ever protects you.'

sanskrit: nyagbhāvaṃ paramaṃ vāyoḥ śalmale tvam upāgataḥ tavāham asmīti sadā yena rakṣati mārutaḥ
english: 'You have come, O silk-cotton tree, into the deepest submission to the wind, so that the wind, as though saying "I am yours," forever protects you.'

sanskrit: na taṃ paśyāmy ahaṃ vṛkṣaṃ parvataṃ vāpi taṃ dṛḍham yo na vāyubalād bhagnaḥ pṛthivyām iti me matiḥ
english: 'I see no tree, nor any mountain however firm, that has not been broken upon the earth by the force of the wind—such is my conviction.'

sanskrit: tvaṃ punaḥ kāraṇair nūnaṃ śalmale rakṣyase sadā vāyunā saparīvāras tena tiṣṭhasy asaṃśayam
english: 'You, then, O silk-cotton tree, are surely protected for some cause; by the wind, with all your retinue, you stand secure beyond doubt.'

sanskrit: śalmalir uvāca na me vāyuḥ sakhā brahman na bandhur na ca me suhṛt parameṣṭhī tathā naiva yena rakṣati mānilaḥ
english: The silk-cotton tree said: The wind is no friend of mine, O brahmin, nor my kinsman, nor my well-wisher, nor my supreme lord, that the wind should protect me out of such regard.

sanskrit: mama tejobalaṃ vāyor bhīmam api hi nārada kalām aṣṭādaśīṃ prāṇair na me prāpnoti mārutaḥ
english: My fiery strength, O Nārada—the wind, terrible though it is, does not by its blasts attain even an eighteenth part of mine.

sanskrit: āgacchan paramo vāyur mayā viṣṭambhito balāt rujan drumān parvatāṃś ca yac cānyad api kiṃ cana
english: When the mighty wind comes rushing on—shattering trees and mountains and whatever else there may be—I check it by my force.

sanskrit: sa mayā bahuśo bhagnaḥ prabhañjan vai prabhañjanaḥ tasmān na bibhye devarṣe kruddhād api samīraṇāt
english: That breaker of all things, the storm-wind itself, has often been broken by me; and so, O divine sage, I do not fear the wind, even in its wrath.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca śalmale viparītaṃ te darśanaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ na hi vāyor balenāsti bhūtaṃ tulyabalaṃ kva cit
english: Nārada said: O silk-cotton tree, your view is perverse, of this there is no doubt; for in strength there is nowhere any being equal to the wind.

sanskrit: indro yamo vaiśravaṇo varuṇaś ca jaleśvaraḥ na te 'pi tulyā marutaḥ kiṃ punas tvaṃ vanaspate
english: Indra, Yama, Vaiśravaṇa, and Varuṇa the lord of waters—not even they are equal to the wind; how much less you, O forest-lord?

sanskrit: yad dhi kiṃ cid iha prāṇi śalmale ceṣṭate bhuvi sarvatra bhagavān vāyuś ceṣṭāprāṇakaraḥ prabhuḥ
english: Whatever living thing stirs here upon the earth, O silk-cotton tree—everywhere it is the blessed wind, the lord, that grants both motion and breath.

sanskrit: eṣa ceṣṭayate samyak prāṇinaḥ samyag āyataḥ asamyag āyato bhūyaś ceṣṭate vikṛto nṛṣu
english: When rightly disposed, it sets living beings rightly in motion; when ill-disposed, it stirs again, working disorder, in men.

sanskrit: sa tvam evaṃvidhaṃ vāyuṃ sarvasattvabhṛtāṃ varam na pūjayasi pūjyaṃ taṃ kim anyad buddhilāghavāt
english: That you do not honor such a wind—best of all that sustains living things, worthy of honor as it is—what is this but lightness of wit?

sanskrit: asāraś cāsi durbuddhe kevalaṃ bahu bhāṣase krodhādibhir avacchanno mithyā vadasi śalmale
english: You are without substance, O fool, and merely babble much; clouded over by anger and the like, you speak falsely, O silk-cotton tree.

sanskrit: mama roṣaḥ samutpannas tvayy evaṃ saṃprabhāṣati bravīmy eṣa svayaṃ vāyos tava durbhāṣitaṃ bahu
english: Anger has risen in me at you, while you talk on like this; I shall myself report to the wind much of your evil speech.

sanskrit: candanaiḥ spandanaiḥ śālaiḥ saralair devadārubhiḥ vetasair bandhanaiś cāpi ye cānye balavattarāḥ
english: By sandal and spandana trees, by śāla, by sarala and deodar, by reed and bandhana, and by others yet stronger still—

sanskrit: taiś cāpi naivaṃ durbuddhe kṣipto vāyuḥ kṛtātmabhiḥ te hi jānanti vāyoś ca balam ātmana eva ca
english: not even by these, O fool, those disciplined ones, is the wind thus reviled; for they know both the wind's strength and their own.

sanskrit: tasmāt te vai namasyanti śvasanaṃ drumasattamāḥ tvaṃ tu mohān na jānīṣe vāyor balam anantakam
english: Therefore those best of trees do homage to the wind; but you, out of delusion, do not know the wind's strength, which has no end.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evam uktvā tu rājendra śalmaliṃ brahmavittamaḥ nāradaḥ pavane sarvaṃ śalmaler vākyam abravīt
english: Bhīṣma said: Having thus spoken to the silk-cotton tree, O lord of kings, Nārada, best of the knowers of brahman, reported to the wind every word the tree had said.

sanskrit: himavatpṛṣṭhajaḥ kaś cic chalmaliḥ parivāravān bṛhanmūlo bṛhacchākhaḥ sa tvāṃ vāyo 'vamanyate
english: 'A certain silk-cotton tree, sprung on the slopes of the Himālaya, with a great following, of mighty root and mighty branch—he, O Wind, holds you in contempt.'

sanskrit: bahūny ākṣepayuktāni tvām āha vacanāni saḥ na yuktāni mayā vāyo tāni vaktuṃ tvayi prabho
english: 'Many insulting words he spoke of you, O Wind; yet it is not fitting for me to repeat them to you, O lord.'

sanskrit: jānāmi tvām ahaṃ vāyo sarvaprāṇabhṛtāṃ varam variṣṭhaṃ ca gariṣṭhaṃ ca krodhe vaivasvataṃ yathā
english: 'I know you, O Wind, to be the best of all that bears the breath of life, most excellent and most weighty, and in wrath like the son of Vivasvat himself.'

sanskrit: evaṃ tu vacanaṃ śrutvā nāradasya samīraṇaḥ śalmaliṃ tam upāgamya kruddho vacanam abravīt
english: Hearing Nārada's words thus, the wind, drawing near to that silk-cotton tree, spoke in anger these words.

sanskrit: śalmale nārade yat tat tvayoktaṃ madvigarhaṇam ahaṃ vāyuḥ prabhāvaṃ te darśayāmy ātmano balam
english: 'O silk-cotton tree, as for that reviling of me which you uttered before Nārada—I, the Wind, shall show you my power, my own strength.'

sanskrit: nāhaṃ tvā nābhijānāmi viditaś cāsi me druma pitāmahaḥ prajāsarge tvayi viśrāntavān prabhuḥ
english: 'It is not that I do not know you—you are well known to me, O tree. At the creation of beings, the Grandfather, the lord, took his rest in you.'

sanskrit: tasya viśramaṇād eva prasādo yaḥ kṛtas tava rakṣyase tena durbuddhe nātmavīryād drumādhama
english: 'It is by that resting of his that the grace shown to you was granted; by that you are protected, O fool—not by your own valor, O basest of trees.'

sanskrit: yan mā tvam avajānīṣe yathānyaṃ prākṛtaṃ tathā darśayāmy eṣa ātmānaṃ yathā mām avabhotsyase
english: 'Since you despise me as though I were some common thing, I shall now show you myself, so that you shall come to know me for what I am.'

sanskrit: evam uktas tataḥ prāha śalmaliḥ prahasann iva pavana tvaṃ vane kruddho darśayātmānam ātmanā
english: Thus addressed, the silk-cotton tree then said, as though laughing: 'O Wind, angered here in the forest, show your self by your own self.'

sanskrit: mayi vai tyajyatāṃ krodhaḥ kiṃ me kruddhaḥ kariṣyasi na te bibhemi pavana yady api tvaṃ svayaṃprabhuḥ
english: 'Let your anger at me be set aside—what will you do to me in your wrath? I do not fear you, O Wind, even though you are your own master.'

sanskrit: ity evam uktaḥ pavanaḥ śva ity evābravīd vacaḥ darśayiṣyāmi te tejas tato rātrir upāgamat
english: So addressed, the wind spoke just this word—'Tomorrow'—'I shall show you my might'; and then the night drew on.

sanskrit: atha niścitya manasā śalmalir vātakāritam paśyamānas tadātmānam asamaṃ mātariśvanaḥ
english: Then the silk-cotton tree, considering in its mind what the wind could do, and seeing that its own self was no match for Mātariśvan,

sanskrit: nārade yan mayā proktaṃ pavanaṃ prati tan mṛṣā asamartho hy ahaṃ vāyor balena balavān hi saḥ
english: thought: 'What I declared to Nārada concerning the wind was false; for I am no match for the wind in strength—strong indeed is he.

sanskrit: māruto balavān nityaṃ yathainaṃ nārado 'bravīt ahaṃ hi durbalo 'nyebhyo vṛkṣebhyo nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: The wind is forever strong, just as Nārada declared him; and I am weaker than the other trees, of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: kiṃ tu buddhyā samo nāsti mama kaś cid vanaspatiḥ tad ahaṃ buddhim āsthāya bhayaṃ mokṣye samīraṇāt
english: Yet in wit no forest-tree is my equal; so, resorting to wit, I shall free myself from the danger of the wind.

sanskrit: yadi tāṃ buddhim āsthāya careyuḥ parṇino vane ariṣṭāḥ syuḥ sadā kruddhāt pavanān nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: If the leaf-bearing trees of the forest were to act with that same wit, they would forever be unharmed by the angry wind, of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: te 'tra bālā na jānanti yathā nainān samīraṇaḥ samīrayeta saṃkruddho yathā jānāmy ahaṃ tathā
english: But here those foolish ones do not know, as I know, how the wind, when greatly enraged, may toss them about.

sanskrit: tato niścitya manasā śalmaliḥ kṣubhitas tadā śākhāḥ skandhān praśākhāś ca svayam eva vyaśātayat
english: Then, having so resolved in its mind, the silk-cotton tree, deeply agitated, of its own accord cast down its branches, its boughs, and its lesser limbs.

sanskrit: sa parityajya śākhāś ca patrāṇi kusumāni ca prabhāte vāyum āyāntaṃ pratyaikṣata vanaspatiḥ
english: Having shed its branches, its leaves, and its blossoms, the forest-lord awaited the coming of the wind at dawn.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddhaḥ śvasan vāyuḥ pātayan vai mahādrumān ājagāmātha taṃ deśaṃ sthito yatra sa śalmaliḥ
english: Then the angry wind, roaring and casting down great trees, came on to that place where the silk-cotton tree stood.
